name: dates: a date the model wrote the way it is said is put back the way a page writes it, when a page it has read holds that day: "November twenty-second" becomes "November 22", "the twenty-second of November" too, a year is kept; a day no page holds is left alone, and so are words that only look like a date ("you may first need", "March first-year students")

texts: The application closes November twenty-second at eleven fifty-nine p.m., which is seven days from today.
Your advisor's own requirements are due later, on December first.
It is due on the twenty-second of November.
by November twenty two at the latest
January the eighth, 2027 is the payment deadline
A late form is taken until November thirtieth.
You may first need to add an officer.
In March first-year students register before everyone else.
